title: Reduce tail latency: OTLP gRPC connection pooling and credential rotation for tracing backends
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent increases in tail latency (p95/p99) for OTLP/gRPC exporter writes to Tempo and Jaeger during brief bursts and tenant churn. Contributing factors: per-request channel creation in the exporter, gRPC TLS handshakes, and occasional blocking when short-lived credentials (STS/KMS tokens) are refreshed mid-write. This ticket implements a connection pooling and credential rotation strategy for the otlp exporter clients used by the trace ingest pipeline to reduce p95/p99 tail latency and connection churn.

Proposed design:
- Maintain a small pool of long-lived gRPC channels per (backend, region) key, reused across exporter threads. Pool size defaults to 2 per backend and is configurable by tenant or global config.
- Use a connection manager that performs: keepalive pinging, TLS session reuse (where supported), and backoff-based reconnection on transient failures.
- Decouple credential refresh from in-flight requests: implement a background refresh task that pre-fetches new short-lived tokens and atomically swaps credentials on channels. If token refresh fails, channels continue using last valid token until expiry threshold with circuit-breaker logic.
- Provide a graceful handoff: existing streams complete while new streams start on channels with refreshed creds. Avoid blocking the exporter main loop during rotation.
- Add exporter-level metrics: active_channel_count, channel_reuse_ratio, credential_refresh_latency, refresh_failures, connection_retry_count, and channel_idle_seconds. Emit per-backend and aggregated tags for dashboarding.
- Add feature flag gating and runtime config so we can roll out to a subset of tenants and easily disable if regressions happen.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pooling increases memory and TLS state but reduces CPU/time per-request. We chose a small default pool to balance resource cost and reuse benefit.
- Background credential refresh slightly increases complexity but avoids request-path blocking. We will keep retry/backoff conservative to avoid token storms.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 and p99 write latency to Tempo/Jaeger reduce by at least 25% for synthetic burst tests compared to baseline.
- No increase in overall error rate for trace ingestion (>1% regression).
- New metrics are emitted and visible in the latency/error dashboard.
- Config knobs and FF exist for rollout, and the feature can be toggled without service restart.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement behind FF and unit tests.
2) Canary rollout in staging with synthetic burst harness measuring p50/p95/p99.
3) Enable for 10% of tenant traffic in production with enhanced tracing and alerts.
4) Gradual ramp to 100% if metrics stable.

Notes: This is scoped to the exporter/gRPC client layer only. Subsequent follow-ups (sub_issues) will evaluate autoscaling and tenant-specific pool sizing heuristics.
